title: How to Create an Email List in Gmail (2026 Guide) | Scrap.io

facts.fact: Scrap.io's page states that there are 25,780,971 businesses on Google Maps in the US, a vendor-supplied figure not attributed to a third-party source.
facts.quote: There are 25,780,971 businesses on Google Maps in the US right now.

facts.fact: Scrap.io's page states that 8,851,466 of the US businesses on Google Maps have a public email address that can be reached, a vendor-supplied figure.
facts.quote: Only 8,851,466 of them have a public email address you can actually reach.

facts.fact: The page says creating a Google Contacts label-based email list (Method 1) takes four minutes and is free.
facts.quote: It takes four minutes and it's free.

facts.fact: The page's comparison table gives a setup time of about 4 minutes for a Gmail contact label, about 15 minutes for a Google Group, and an afternoon for a dedicated tool.
facts.quote: | Setup time | ~4 minutes | ~15 minutes | An afternoon |

facts.fact: The page's comparison table states that unsubscribe handling is manual for a Gmail contact label, self-service for a Google Group, and automatic for a dedicated tool.
The page states that Gmail has no feature called an email list.
facts.quote: Gmail doesn't have a feature called "email list." It never has.

facts.fact: The page states that when a contact label is placed in the To field, every recipient can see every other recipient's address, while placing it in Bcc hides recipients from each other but limits replies to the sender.
facts.quote: Put the label in the **To** field and every recipient sees every other address.
